# Closest Wins

A Skill Harbor house build: Closest Wins, the numeric estimation game, refereed by your own Muse. The referee asks a question whose answer is a number, in a named unit: how tall, how far, how many, in what year counted how. Everyone gives one number, and the closest to the true value scores 1 point. The default game is 5 rounds, and the skill is not about knowing the figure: every question passes a quality gate that keeps only stable, verifiable facts that nobody knows by heart but anyone can approach by order of magnitude reasoning, with no famous figure recited from school and no clue hidden in the wording.

The fairness is in the sealing. Before the first question is asked, every round's true value is written into the game state file, with its source in one line: that sealed key never leaves the file before its round's reveal, and a value is never corrected quietly mid-round; a fact discovered false cancels its round, with no points, and the game moves on. Play solo in chat, against a sealed tolerance written before the game, 20 percent by default and never adjusted after an answer: land within it and you score the point. Or play in a group, 2 players and more, inside a group chat you own: answers are collected in private, one to one, because a visible number anchors everyone after it, and the reveal publishes the true value, all the answers, every distance and the running scores all at once. The closest scores 1 point, an exact answer scores the same single point and is...
